Prague was still 500 miles or so distant - it was a long night. Torben Betts’ play rakes over some very, very well worn theories (never more than a click or two away from where you are right now in the Internet Age) about the assassination of John F Kennedy, The Mob connections of Lee Harvey Oswald and the tragic death of Marilyn Monroe.
Ultimately, the play acts to speculate on Kilgallen’s original theories.
Speculations is an absorbing piece of theatre, anchored by a compelling central performance from Janie Dee and framed by a set of rare ambition.

Despite a few written missteps and monotonous structure, Speculations is a fascinating watch that gives you the chance to flex your true crime muscles, and embrace all of your conspiracy theories just like Dorothy Kilgallen.
The play draws you into the conspiracies none of which are new revelations but the structure of the play works well at introducing the theoretical basis.
Speculations doesn't quite live up to its promise and stops short of connecting the dots between these cases.
An interesting, if flawed evening of theatre that leaves us with plenty of questions but not enough dramatic satisfaction.

While these conspiracy theories will undoubtedly continue to be revisited for years to come, Speculations doesn’t add anything new to the story beyond the dramatisation of Dorothy Kilgallen, whose own theories ultimately don’t stand up to scrutiny.

Ultimately, it feels like a shame that the play does not quite fulfil its potential, as it could have left audiences genuinely curious and emotionally engaged, rather than simply presenting them with a set of seemingly predetermined conclusions.
Overall, a very glossy production, superbly performed with seriously intriguing content that will grip you all the way through.
Kilgallen is shrewd, witty and unrelenting, in a masterful performance by Dee.
All they are likely to question is why they bought a ticket.
But the trouble with Speculations is that very little feels new.
Ultimately, SPECULATIONS squanders a fascinating historical premise with sluggish pacing and flat writing that even a dedicated cast can't save.
Unfortunately the skills of a talented group of actors are not enough to lift this material into an engaging watch.

cn.t: Critics are sharply divided on this conspiracy thriller, with praise for Janie Dee's performance and ambitious design undercut by widespread criticism of a clumsy script and implausible premise that fails to justify revisiting JFK and Marilyn theories.
